title: Canonical point-family comparison and the Q-evaluation counit for the coherent nerve of Kan complexes
statement:
Use the coherent nerve and simplicial category of Kan complexes of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], the right-pinched and internal mapping conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the cosimplicial resolution $Q$, coend $V$, map $p$, and evaluation counit of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]. Work in universes containing all the displayed objects. Put $\mathcal S=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan})$. For Kan complexes $X,Y$, write $T_{X,Y}=\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)$, $R_{X,Y}=\operatorname{Map}^R_{\mathcal S}(X,Y)$ and $U_{X,Y}=U_{\mathcal S}(X,Y)$, with $j:R_{X,Y}\to U_{X,Y}$ as in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. There is a natural isomorphism
$$R_{X,Y}\cong\operatorname{Sing}_Q T_{X,Y}.$$
It sends a map $J^n\to\mathcal S$ to the induced enriched morphism map $Q^n\to T_{X,Y}$. Under this isomorphism, let $E_{X,Y}:V(R_{X,Y})\to T_{X,Y}$ be the evaluation counit, whose restriction to the summand indexed by $\sigma:J^n\to\mathcal S$ is that induced map. Equivalently, $E_{X,Y}$ is the composite of $\theta_{\mathcal S,X,Y}$ with the enriched adjunction counit $\mathfrak C[N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathbf{Kan}](X,Y)\to\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)$, which evaluates an enriched simplex in $\mathbf{Kan}$.

Let $q^n:Q^n\to\Delta^n$ be the cosimplicial maximum map: on a subset $B$ in the subset-poset presentation of a morphism from an initial vertex to the final vertex $n+1$, it is $\max(B\setminus\{n+1\})$; it descends after the initial face is collapsed. The maps $\alpha_{X,Y}:T_{X,Y}\to R_{X,Y}$ defined by $t\mapsto t q^n$ in degree $n$, and $\beta_{X,Y}=j\alpha_{X,Y}:T_{X,Y}\to U_{X,Y}$, are homotopy equivalences. In the ordinary localization of simplicial sets at weak homotopy equivalences,
$$[E_{X,Y}]=[\alpha_{X,Y}]^{-1}[p_{R_{X,Y}}].$$
The comparison $\beta$ respects enriched composition, identities, and precomposition by a point $\eta:*\to X$, up to homotopies on the entire mapping spaces, natural in additional simplicial parameters. In particular this precomposition corresponds to $\operatorname{ev}_\eta:T_{X,Y}\to Y=T_{*,Y}$.

For any small simplicial set $K$, use the degreewise currying isomorphism $U_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)}(\Delta_K X,\Delta_K Y)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,U_{X,Y})$. Postcomposition with $\beta_{X,Y}$, together with the right-pinch comparison in the functor category, gives the specified natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}^R_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)}(\Delta_KX,\Delta_KY)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,T_{X,Y}).$$
At $X=*$ this is a choice of the point-family equivalence of [lem-coef-space-point-cocone-criterion]: for an edge cocone with adjoint arrow family $\gamma:K\to U_{*,Y}$, its point map is any simplicial representative of $[\beta_{*,Y}]^{-1}[\gamma]$. These assertions retain all faces and degeneracies, are natural under enriched functors wherever the displayed inputs apply, and are unchanged on passing to a containing universe.

source.place: Section 2.2.4 opening paragraph before Proposition 2.2.4.1, printed p. 88 (PDF page 106), for the enriched Q-counit formula. Kerodon Example 4.6.7.7 (06QR) and Remark 4.6.7.6 for the canonical enriched mapping comparison, and Definition 5.6.6.1 (038A) for evaluation at a point. The maximum/prism and constant-diagram normalization are agent formulations of these comparisons; no Stacks tag states this result. Sources read online; archival extracts WANTED.

proof.text: Work in a containing universe throughout. The internal mapping complexes $T_{X,Y}=\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)$ are Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan]. Thus [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory] applies to the simplicial category $\mathbf{Kan}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces] and makes $\mathcal S$ a quasicategory. The right-pinch comparison then makes $R_{X,Y}$ and $U_{X,Y}$ Kan and supplies the specified homotopy equivalence $j:R_{X,Y}\to U_{X,Y}$. These facts apply also when a mapping space is empty.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion: Kan hypotheses for the concrete space category and its mapping objects

proof.text: A map $J^n\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathbf{Kan}$ is equivalently an enriched functor $\mathfrak C[J^n]\to\mathbf{Kan}$: on every simplex this is the coherent-nerve definition, and compatibility on all simplices is the universal property of the simplex colimit defining $\mathfrak C$. The source has two objects, identity endomorphism spaces, no reverse morphisms, and sole nonidentity mapping space $Q^n$; collapsing the initial face makes all its arrows identities. Fixing the endpoint images $X,Y$ therefore leaves exactly the datum of a map $Q^n\to T_{X,Y}$. Restriction along a monotone map acts on this datum by precomposition with the corresponding $Q$-operator. This gives the asserted natural simplicial isomorphism $R_{X,Y}\cong\operatorname{Sing}_Q T_{X,Y}$. Under it, evaluation on a summand indexed by $\sigma:J^n\to\mathcal S$ is the induced map $Q^n\to T_{X,Y}$, so it is precisely the evaluation counit $E_{X,Y}$ of the resolution node. That node's summand formula for $\theta$, followed by the enriched adjunction counit (which evaluates the enriched simplex), gives the very same map on each summand and hence the equivalent formula for $E$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion: HTT 2.2.4 opening paragraph: identification with the actual Q evaluation counit

proof.text: For a subset $B$ in a morphism from $i\leq n$ to $n+1$, put $q^n(B)=\max(B\setminus\{n+1\})$. Union with a subset in the initial face ending at $i$ adds only elements at most $i$ and hence leaves that maximum unchanged. Sending every initial-face arrow to an identity therefore respects composition and descends across the collapse to $Q^n$. The maximum is monotone on subset inclusions, and $\max(aI)=a(\max I)$ for every monotone $a:[m]\to[n]$, including noninjective ones. Thus $q$ is cosimplicial. For the cosimplicial map $p$ furnished by the resolution, set $r^n=\max(p^n,q^n)$ vertexwise. This defines a simplicial map to the ordinal nerve $\Delta^n$. The inequalities $p^n\leq r^n\geq q^n$ give a natural zigzag of simplicial homotopies: on each simplex, use the smaller value before the interval parameter switches and the larger value afterwards. Monotone ordinal maps preserve maxima, so these homotopies commute with every $Q$-operator. Products with $\Delta^1$ preserve the coend quotient degreewise, giving $p_A\simeq r_A\simeq q_A$ for every $A$. The Kan-target criterion implies two-out-of-three for weak equivalences and says homotopic maps are weak equivalences simultaneously: their precomposition maps agree on edge-components. Since $p_A$ is a weak equivalence, so is $q_A$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion: explicit maximum map and comparison with the resolution augmentation

proof.text: Under Step 2 define $\alpha:T\to R$ in degree $n$ by $t\mapsto tq^n$; cosimplicial naturality makes it simplicial. Evaluating on every coend summand gives the strict equation $EV(\alpha)=q_T$. Both $E$ (because $T$ is Kan) and $q_T$ are weak equivalences, so $V(\alpha)$ is one. Naturality of $p$ gives $p_RV(\alpha)=\alpha p_T$; since both $p_R,p_T$ are weak equivalences, two-out-of-three makes $\alpha$ a weak equivalence. It has an actual simplicial homotopy inverse. Indeed the Kan-target criterion applied to $\alpha$, with test target $T$, gives $g:R\to T$ such that $g\alpha$ is in the edge-component of $1_T$. Its injectivity with test target $R$ then gives $\alpha g$ in the component of $1_R$. The relevant internal functor objects are Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan]. In a Kan complex an edge can be reversed by an outer two-horn with an identity, and two edges composed by an inner two-horn. Hence every finite edge zigzag compresses to one edge, giving the two required simplicial homotopies. Composing with the homotopy equivalence $j$ proves that $\beta=j\alpha$ is a homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion: weak equivalence and actual homotopy-inverse construction for alpha and beta

proof.text:
Simplicially homotopic maps become equal in the ordinary localization used in the statement. To see this without identifying that localization with an unspecified homotopy category, the projection $A\times\Delta^1\to A$ has a section at $0$ and a simplicial contraction given on the interval factor by $\min(s,t)$. It is a simplicial homotopy equivalence, hence a weak equivalence by [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak]. Both endpoint inclusions consequently become its unique inverse in the localization. Apply this observation to the zigzag in Step 3 to obtain $[q_T]=[p_T]$. Since $[V(\alpha)]$ is invertible by Step 4, the strict equations there now give
$$[E]=[q_T][V(\alpha)]^{-1}=[p_T][V(\alpha)]^{-1}=[\alpha]^{-1}[p_R].$$
This is the asserted equation for the actual counit, with the inverse of the specified $\alpha$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion: calculation of the counit in the specified ordinary localization

proof.text: Write $b=\beta$. For an $n$-simplex $f:\Delta^n\to T_{X,Y}$, its prism $b(f)$ has identity arrows within each layer of $[1]\times[n]$; on a subset $B$ crossing from layer $0$ to layer $1$, its enriched map is $f(s)$ with $s$ the largest parameter among the layer-$0$ vertices. Indeed the pinch sends all layer-$1$ vertices to $n+1$, and $q$ takes the maximum of the remaining vertices. For $g:\Delta^n\to T_{Y,Z}$, define a map $\Phi(g,f):\Delta^2\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal S$ on each chain of $[2]\times[n]$ as follows. Send layers to $X,Y,Z$ and within-layer arrows to identities. On subsets joining $0$ to $1$ use $f$ at the largest layer-$0$ parameter, and on subsets joining $1$ to $2$ use $g$ at the largest layer-$1$ parameter. On a subset joining $0$ to $2$, use $g(t)\circ f(s)$, where $s$ is the largest layer-$0$ parameter and $t$ the largest parameter in layers $0,1$. These are monotone functions of the subset. Splitting at a layer-$1$ vertex recovers precisely these two maxima, so enriched composition is union-composition; splitting within an outer layer only inserts an identity. The formulas therefore give enriched functors, agree on common faces of chains, and define $\Phi$ simplicially. Its edges are $b(f),b(g),b(g\circ f)$; on the $02$ face one has $s=t$. Thus for the triangle-space maps of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], $\theta\Phi=b\times b$ and $\ell\Phi=b\circ\mathrm{comp}$. Since $\theta$ is a homotopy equivalence, that node's formula proves compatibility with coherent composition on the entire mapping complexes.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion: explicit three-layer prism for enriched composition

proof.text: Constant identity maps in the prism formula of Step 6 give degenerate identity edges, and its two outer composition specializations give the unit homotopies. Take $f=\eta:*\to X$ constant in that formula. Enriched composition with it is strictly evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_\eta:T_{X,Y}\to T_{*,Y}=Y$. Consequently the composition compatibility just proved identifies coherent precomposition by the edge $\eta$ with this evaluation map up to homotopy on the whole mapping space. Each maximum formula commutes with every monotone change of parameter. Further simplicial parameters may therefore be retained throughout the prism construction; its homotopies are homotopies of maps, not merely equalities on components. Applying any enriched functor to all the displayed enriched maps preserves their union-composition and identities, so $\alpha,\beta,E$ and these comparison homotopies have the asserted enriched naturality wherever those inputs apply.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion: identity, point evaluation, and naturality of the explicit comparison

proof.text:
The functor quasicategory $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)$ is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. An $n$-simplex of $U_D(\Delta_KX,\Delta_KY)$ is exactly a map $K\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal S$ with its endpoint restrictions constant at $X,Y$. Currying gives the stated degreewise isomorphism with $\operatorname{Fun}(K,U_{X,Y})$, respecting all operators. If $g$ is a homotopy inverse to $\beta$, postcomposition with $g$ and $\beta$ gives inverse homotopy equivalences on these internal functor objects: evaluate their homotopies at every point of $K$ with the same interval parameter. Combining this with the homotopy equivalence $j_D$ gives the specified natural zigzag
$$\operatorname{Map}^R_D(\Delta_KX,\Delta_KY)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(K,U_{X,Y})\longleftarrow\operatorname{Fun}(K,T_{X,Y}).$$
At $X=*$ this constructs a choice of the point-family comparison of [lem-coef-space-point-cocone-criterion]. More explicitly, for the adjoint arrow family $\gamma:K\to U_{*,Y}$ its point map is $g\gamma:K\to Y$. The two homotopy-inverse equations give $[g\gamma]=[\beta_{*,Y}]^{-1}[\gamma]$ and independence up to homotopy of the inverse chosen. No normalization of an inverse beyond this displayed construction is taken from the criterion node.

source.place: Paragraph 2, agent expansion: constant-diagram currying and the actual point-family normalization

proof.text: Every displayed identification is degreewise: simplex restriction gives the operators on $R$, precomposition gives those on $\operatorname{Sing}_Q$, evaluation descends through the coend relations, and the maximum and three-layer formulas commute with monotone maps. Currying is also degreewise. The resulting equivalence is consequently an equivalence of entire mapping spaces, retains faces and degeneracies, and is natural under restriction in $K$ and enriched changes of the displayed inputs. The identity and composition homotopies in Step 7 supply naturality for point precomposition as well. Empty $K$ gives one-point internal functor objects and the same zigzag; empty enriched mapping spaces give empty $R,U$ in Step 2. Finally, enlarging the containing universe changes none of the displayed simplicial sets, formulas, or their inverse homotopies. Those inverse homotopies still prove the asserted equivalences, and the same formal-localization equation follows from the same homotopies there. This proves universe independence without asserting that the collection of all small spaces stays the same.
